verdict: Visually clear and carefully qualified on desktop and mobile. No release-blocking clipping, per-race/aggregate confusion, or accuracy claim found.

observations.hierarchy: The expected wrong-top-choice and expected average-margin-error cards are distinct, with the 35-race denominator visible. Method definitions, joint-row coverage and signed-error caveats are in a clear disclosure. The selected-race view states ‘Awaiting verified result’ and gives its own 4.2 pp model-implied expected error separately from the 5.6 pp aggregate.
observations.interpretation: Copy says the values are from the model's own probabilities/simulations, not measured accuracy or error limits. It explicitly says 5.6 pp is not a per-race range, explains equal race weighting, names the two-contender conditional target, and rejects full-ballot and national popular-vote readings. The definitions view explains shared rows, no independence reconstruction, interval width plus misses, signed-error direction, the centered-by-construction caveat, no results, and no grade.
observations.mobile: All three mobile screens are readable, cards stack naturally, uncertainty and selected-race text wrap within the viewport, and no visible clipping or horizontal overflow appears. The longer definitions disclosure remains scannable with separate headings and paragraphs.
observations.confidence_and_accuracy: ‘The model expects’ is immediately qualified as its own simulated distribution. ‘Middle 90%’ is paired with explicit range values and the disclosure says internal reference, not evidence of real-world coverage. There is no unsupported predictive-skill claim or grade.

small_copy_refinements.reason: ‘Shared errors’ is slightly technical; naming shared shifts is more concrete while preserving dependence.

small_copy_refinements.suggestion: The model's 5th–95th percentile range across simulated 35-race averages is 4.0 to 7.9 points.
small_copy_refinements.reason: This makes the percentile interpretation self-contained in the first view. Existing nearby copy already rules out a per-race band and 95% confidence interval, so this is a clarity improvement only.
